panels.rationale: Histology panel from a patient with floor-of-mouth dermoid cyst; caption and in-text explicitly describe the cystic structure lined by hyperplastic squamous mucosa with adnexal/sebaceous structures, supporting direct disease attribution.
panels.attribution_text: Patel et al. Marsupialization of a Floor-of-Mouth Dermoid Cyst to Temporize Airway Distress.. Cureus 2022. doi:10.7759/cureus.22781. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: High-powered image of pathology slide of surgical specimen demonstrating a cystic structure lined by hyperplastic squamous mucosa containing focal adnexal structures with mural fibrosis, chronic inflammation, and focal intraepithelial acute inflammation.
in_text_mentions: Surgical pathology sections demonstrate a cyst lined by hyperplastic squamous mucosa. The wall of the cyst contained focal adnexal structures including sebaceous glands and scattered foci of smooth muscle fascicles with mural fibrosis, chronic inflammation, and focal intraepithelial acute inflammation. These findings are consistent with a benign oral dermoid autogenic cyst (Fig. 3). Adnexal structures, such as sebaceous glands, were also identified interspersed with scattered foci of smooth muscle fascicles.
